correctness.rationale: Reverse preimages a^-1 rotate cyclic intervals and b^-1 can grow a nonfull interval only when it is {0,...,r-1}; each growth adds n-1 and requires n-1 inverse a-rotations before the next growth. Growing a singleton to all n states requires n-1 effective b actions, yielding the minimum L and its rigid unique word. One extra a must occur before forward W (after reverse set fills Q); one extra b must be an identity inverse insertion because any shrink loses too much. In the jth internal gap the only forbidden insertion offset is t=j; summing n-2 offsets for each of n-2 gaps gives (n-2)^2 plus aW. Wa,Wb are the two already-reset extensions, giving total (n-2)^2+3. Independent bit-mask subset dynamic programming verified no earlier resets, exactly one at L and the first-next counts 1,2,5,10,17,26,37,50,65,82 for n=2..11. Algebraic proof, not finite DP, justifies all n.

final_claim: For the labeled n-state Černý automaton n≥2, the shortest reset word W=b(a^(n-1)b)^(n-2) is unique, length L=(n-1)^2; exactly (n-2)^2+1 words of length L+1 first reset at their final letter and (n-2)^2+3 words of length L+1 reset at or before the final letter; every first-final word is explicitly listed.
limitations: Exactly (n-1)^2+1 letters, n≥2; distinction between first-final reset and already reset earlier preserved.
